parts.text:
Ravi, ye store ka charge ab mere paas hai. Inventory kahan se shuru karein?

Madam, GFR 2017 ka Chapter 7. Rule 207 se 223 tak — poori kahani isi mein hai.

Toh pehle rule, phir register. Receipt → Custody → Verification → Disposal.

GFR 2017 ka Chapter 7 = Inventory Management, Rule 207 se Rule 223 tak — kul 17 rules. Ye basic rules sab Central Ministries/Departments par lagte hain; aur isi chapter ke hisaab se hi koi bhi Ministry/Department apne detailed instructions bana sakti hai. Inventory sirf "ginti" nahi — 4 kadam: Receipt → Custody → Physical Verification → Disposal.

Madam, supplier ka maal aa gaya. Challan match ho gaya — bas entry kar deta hoon.

Challan kaafi nahi, Ravi. Rule 208 — count, measure ya weigh, visual inspection, phir stock register mein entry.

Aur jab ye samaan doosre division ya contractor ko jayega?

Rule 208 — Private supplier se maal aate hi: contract terms ke hisaab se receipt, phir counting/measuring/weighing + visual inspection (zaroorat par technical inspection), IT-based stock register mein entry, aur officer ka receipt certificate. Rule 209 — internal issue: prescribed form mein indent zaroori + likhit ya online acknowledgement; contractor ko diya gaya maal ho to recovery rate aur total value usse date ke saath sign karwana hoga. Rule 210 — Custody: valuable items aur aag pakadne wale articles ki safe custody, storage ka proper intezaam, temperature control aur dust-free rakhna.

Farah, ye registers alag-alag kyun rakhe hain — ek hi kyun nahi?

Kyunki Rule 211 kehta hai — har category ka alag account. Fixed assets GFR-22, consumables GFR-23, historical/artistic GFR-24.

Aur jo purana genset contractor ko hire par gaya — uska record aur hire charges?

Rule 211 — Officer-in-charge ko item-wise lists aur accurate returns rakhne honge, taaki kisi bhi time actual balance aur book balance check ho sake. Register ka format 3 cheezon par depend karta hai — goods ki nature, transactions ki frequency aur department ki requirements. Alag-alag category ke liye alag account: Fixed assets Form GFR-22, consumables GFR-23, library books GFR-18, historical/artistic value assets GFR-24. Rule 212 — Agar fixed asset kisi local body, contractor ya aur kisi ko hire par diya jaaye, to proper record rakhna hoga, hire aur dusre charges regularly recover karne honge, aur charges ka calculation asset ki historical cost par based hoga.

Aaj physical verification hai. Rule 213 — fixed assets aur consumables, dono saal mein kam se kam ek baar.

Verification hamesha custodian officer ke saamne hoga — aur certificate stock register mein.

Aur shortfall ya damage mile to?

Rule 213(1) — Fixed assets ka inventory generally site par rakha jaaye; verification kam se kam saal mein ek baar, outcome corresponding register mein darj, aur discrepancies तुरंत investigate karke account mein layi jayen. Rule 213(2) — Sab consumable goods ka physical verification bhi kam se kam saal mein ek baar; discrepancies stock register mein darj kar action ke liye competent authority ko deni hongi. Verification hamesha custodian officer ke saamne ho, aur verification certificate findings ke saath stock register mein record ho. Verification mein mili shortage, damage ya unserviceable goods तुरंत competent authority ke notice mein layi jayen — Rules 33 se 38 ke hisaab se action ke liye.

Madam, ye A4 paper aur toner pichhle 14 mahine se shelf par pada hai.

Rule 214 ka note yaad rakho — ek saal se zyada stock mein pada material generally surplus maana jaata hai. Buffer stock alag baat hai.

Library alag hai — 20,000 tak volumes ho to har saal poori verification, 50,000 tak 3 saal mein, usse upar sample verification.

Rule 214 — Buffer stock: requirement ki frequency, quantity aur supply pattern ke hisaab se optimum buffer stock competent authority tay karega. Note: inventory carrying cost ek aisa kharch hai jo material ki value nahi badhata — isliye ek saal se zyada time tak stock mein pada material generally surplus maana jayega, jab tak usko alag treat karne ki solid wajah na ho. Aise declared surplus items ko Rule 217 ke procedure se deal kiya jaata hai. Rule 215 — Library books: 20,000 ya usse kam volumes wale library mein har saal complete verification; 20,000 se zyada aur 50,000 tak — kam se kam 3 saal mein ek baar complete verification; 50,000 se zyada — 3 saal se zyada interval par sample verification. Sample verification mein unusual ya unreasonable shortage dikhe to complete verification hogi. Ek saal mein issue/consult ki gayi har 1,000 volumes par 5 volumes ki loss reasonable maani ja sakti hai, agar dishonesty ya negligence ki wajah na ho; lekin ₹1,000 se zyada value ki kitab aur rare books — value chahe jo ho — ki loss ki investigation zaroori hai.

Main transfer ho rahi hoon. Store ka charge aage kaun sambhalega?

Rule 216 — relieving aur relieved officer milkar ek statement banayenge, dono date ke saath sign karenge.

Aur dono ke paas ek-ek copy rahegi — tabhi accountability clear hai.

Rule 216 — Transfer of charge of goods and materials: agar officer-in-charge transfer ho, to transfer hone wale officer ko dekhna hoga ki goods/materials sahi tareeke se uske successor ko hand over diye jayen. Goods aur materials ki sab relevant details ka ek statement banega, jise relieving officer aur relieved officer dono date ke saath sign karenge. Dono officers apne paas signed statement ki ek-ek copy rakhenge. Ye chhota sa rule hai, lekin isi se yah tay hota hai ki agla shortfall kiske account mein jayega.

In purane computers ko "bekaar" likh dena kaafi hai kya?

Nahi Sir. Rule 217 — item kharidne wale competent authority ko reasons record karne honge, aur committee bana sakte hain.

Book value, guiding price, reserved price — teeno nikalenge, aur report Form GFR-10 mein banegi.

Rule 217 — Disposal of goods: kisi item ko surplus, obsolete ya unserviceable tab declare kiya ja sakta hai jab woh Ministry/Department ke kaam ka na rahe. Declare karne ke reasons us authority ko record karne honge jo item kharidne ke liye competent hai. Competent authority apne discretion se committee bana sakti hai. Disposal se pehle book value, guiding price aur reserved price nikalne honge — agar book value nikalna sambhav na ho to original purchase price use kiya ja sakta hai — aur stores ki report Form GFR-10 mein banegi. Agar item kisi government servant ki negligence, fraud ya mischief se unserviceable hua ho, to responsibility fix karni hogi. Hazardous waste, scrap batteries aur e-waste ke liye Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change ke guidelines ke hisaab se sale hogi, aur bidder ke paas e-auction aur delivery ke din valid recycler/pre-processor registration hona chahiye.

Sir, purane furniture ki residual value ₹5.6 lakh aayi hai. Seedhe scrap dealer ko bech den?

Nahi. Rule 218 — ₹4 lakh se upar ho to advertised tender ya public auction hi chalega. Committee decide nahi kar sakti.

Par hamare purane note mein ₹2 lakh likha tha...

Rule 218 — Modes of disposal: assessed residual value ₹4 lakh se upar ho to disposal advertised tender ya public auction se hoga. ₹4 lakh se kam residual value wale goods ke liye mode competent authority tay karega — ismein dhyan rakha jayega ki samaan jama na ho, jagah block na ho, aur value kharab na ho; Ministries/Departments ko aise goods ki list banana chahiye. Expired medicines, food grain, ammunition jaise hazardous ya human consumption ke layak na hone wale goods ko तुरंत suitable mode se dispose ya destroy karein — health hazard, environmental pollution aur misuse se bachne ke liye. Currency, negotiable instruments, receipt books, stamps, security press jaise security concern wale goods/documents ko official secrets rules aur financial prudence ke hisaab se dispose/destroy karein. Dhyan dein: ye threshold ₹2 lakh se badhakar ₹4 lakh kiya gaya — Department of Expenditure ke OM F.1/3/2024-PPD, dated 10.07.2024 se.

Advertised tender ho ya auction — transparency, competition, fairness, discretion ka khatma. Ye chaar principle dono mein common hain.

Farq number ka hai — tender mein bid security 10% of assessed/reserved price; auction mein earnest money 25% of bid value, mauke par.

Aur auction team mein Internal Finance Wing ka officer hona hi chahiye.

Rule 219 — Disposal through advertised tender: bidding documents banana, tender invite karna, bids kholna, evaluate karna, highest responsive bidder chunna, sale value collect karna, sale release order dena, goods release karna, aur aakhir mein unsuccessful bidders ki bid security wapas karna — ye nau kadam (a) se (i) hain; aakhri step aksar bhool jaate hain. Bid document mein goods ki location aur present condition likhni hogi taaki bidder inspect kar sake. Bid security generally assessed ya reserved price ka 10% hogi. Highest acceptable responsive bidder ko hi accept kiya jayega; negotiation sirf usi bidder se ho sakti hai, aur fail hone par agli highest responsive bidder ko reasonable price counter-offer ho sakti hai. Bid security adjust karke baaki poori rakam goods release karne se pehle leni hogi; default par bid security forfeit hogi aur goods defaulter ke risk and cost par dobara beche jayenge. Late bids consider nahi honge.

Rule 220 — Auction: Ministry/Department direct ya approved auctioneer ke through auction kara sakti hai; auction plan ka wide publicity; auction shuru hone par goods ki condition, location aur terms dobara announce karna; bid accept hote hi bid value ka kam se kam 25% earnest money तुरंत mauke par — cash ya Deposit-at-Call-Receipt (DACR) mein — lena; balance payment ke baad hi goods hand over karna; aur auction team mein Internal Finance Wing ka officer hona chahiye.

Tender bhi laga, auction bhi — koi kharidar nahi mila. Ab?

Rule 221 — scrap value par bech sakte hain, competent authority ki approval se aur Finance division se consultation ke baad. Phir bhi na bike to eco-friendly destruction.

Aur write-off alag hai — Rule 223. Sanction tab bhi chahiye jab accounts mein koi adjustment ho ya na ho.

Rule 221 — Agar advertised tender aur auction dono ke bawajood item nahi bikta, to competent authority ki approval se aur Finance division ke saath consultation karke scrap value par becha ja sakta hai. Agar scrap value par bhi na bike, to kisi aur mode se dispose kiya ja sakta hai — jismein eco-friendly destruction bhi shaamil hai. Rule 222 — Dispose kiye gaye goods ka sale account Form GFR-11 mein banega, jis par sale ya auction ki supervision karne wale officer ke sign honge. Rule 223 — Revaluation, stock-taking ya dusri wajah se hone wale profit/loss record kiya jayega aur zaroorat padne par adjust kiye jayenge. Accounts mein koi correction/adjustment shamil na ho, tab bhi loss ke liye competent authority ki formal sanction leni hogi. Write-off ki powers DFPR ke under hain. Depreciation ki wajah se hone wale loss ke chaar heads hain: market price ka normal fluctuation, normal wear and tear, purchases regulate karne mein foresight ki kami, aur kharid ke baad negligence.

Depreciation ke alawa loss ke paanch heads hain: theft ya fraud, neglect, obsolescence ya zaroorat se zyada kharid ki anticipated loss, damage, aur Force Majeure — jaise aag, baadh, ya enemy action. Aakhir mein: abhi ke orders bhi yaad rakhein — DoE ne 10.07.2024 ke OM se disposal threshold ₹2 lakh se ₹4 lakh kiya, aur DARPG ka Special Campaign 6.0 15-30 September 2026 preparation phase, 2-31 October 2026 implementation phase mein chal raha hai, jismein scrap disposal GFR ke hisaab se aur e-waste disposal E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 ke hisaab se karna hai.

Rule 207 — Inventory Management — scope of the chapter. Yaad rakho: Basic rules sabke liye, detail department ki, par Chapter 7 ke hisaab se. Ye rule poore chapter ka "scope clause" hai — isme koi sub-rule, clause ya proviso nahi hai. Ye batata hai ki Chapter 7 ke basic rules kis par lagte hain aur departmental instructions ki kya hadd hai. Rule 207: Do baatein: (1) is chapter ke basic rules sab Ministries/Departments par lagte hain; (2) koi bhi Ministry/Department apne detailed instructions aur procedures bana sakta hai — lekin woh "broadly in conformity" hone chahiye, yaani Chapter 7 ke basic rules ke khilaf nahi ja sakte. Exam trap: Kya koi department Chapter 7 se hat kar apne inventory rules bana sakta hai? Nahi. Detailed instructions "broadly in conformity" with Chapter 7 hone chahiye — conformity test Rule 207 ka core hai.

Rule 208 — Receipt of goods and materials from private suppliers. Yaad rakho: C.I.R.T.S. — Contract, Inspect, Record, Technical check, Stock register. Rule 208 mein sirf ek sub-rule hai — Rule 208(1) — jiske andar teen clauses (i), (ii), (iii) hain. Ye tab lagta hai jab maal bahar ke private supplier se aata hai (internal division se aane par Rule 209 lagega). Rule 208(1): Heading clause. Iske niche (i) se (iii) teen mandatory steps hain — contract dekho, verify karo, register karo. Clause (i): Sabse pehla kadam contract terms padhna hai. Delivery schedule, specification, inspection clause, packaging, insurance — jo kuch contract mein likha hai, receipt usi ke hisaab se honi chahiye. Contract ke bina receipt matlab aage chalkar dispute mein department kamzor padega. Clause (ii): Teen physical cheezein har baar honi chahiye: counting, measuring ya weighing, aur visual inspection — aur ye sab receipt ke time par hi. Visual inspection ke teen objective hain: quantity sahi hai, quality specification ke hisaab se hai, aur koi damage/deficiency nahi. Note: Rule 208 mein koi footnote ya proviso nahi hai — poora rule teen clauses ka hai. Exam trap: Technical inspection kab karwani hogi? "Where required" — jahan zaroori ho, approved Technical Inspector ya approved Agency se. Har baar nahi.

Rule 209 — Receipt / issue of goods and materials from internal divisions of the same organisation. Yaad rakho: Indent → Examine → Acknowledge → (na mile to) entry in indentor copy. Rule 209 mein chaar clauses hain: (i) internal division se maal mangwana, (ii) stock se maal dena, (iii) contractor ko diye gaye maal ki recovery acknowledgement, aur (iv) poora indent pura na kar sakein to kya karna hai — ye last clause sabse zyada ignore hota hai. Clause (i): Maal mangwane wala officer (indenting officer) prescribed form mein indent dega. Maal milne par woh khud examine/count/measure/weigh karega — quantity, quality, damage — teen check Rule 208(ii) jaisi hi hain. Clause (ii): Stock se maal nikalne ka rule: Officer-in-charge ensure karega ki prescribed form ka indent pehle hi maujood hai. Uske baad maal issue karte waqt likhit ya online acknowledgement lena hoga — indenting officer ya uske authorised representative se, aur woh bhi issue ke time par. Note: Rule 209 ke (i) mein receipt SHALL hai jabki Rule 208(iii) mein supplier ko receipt dena MAY hai — ye contrast yaad rakhiye. Exam trap: Contractor ko diya gaya maal — acknowledgement mein kya likhwana zaroori hai? Sirf receipt nahi — recovery rates aur total value chargeable, contractor se signed aur dated.

Rule 210 — Custody of goods and materials. Yaad rakho: Safe custody + Storage + Temperature + Dust-free = Rule 210. Rule 210 ek single-paragraph rule hai — koi sub-rule ya clause nahi. Chhota par bhaari: yahi rule storage ki physical responsibility tay karta hai, aur isi ke na-manne se aksar Rules 33–38 ke loss cases bante hain. Rule 210: Jis officer ke paas samaan ki custody hai, woh chaar cheezein ensure karega: (1) safe custody — security, lock, access control; (2) proper storage accommodation — jagah, racks, handling; (3) required temperature; (4) dust-free environment. Note: Rule 210 mein "etc." hai — matlab temperature aur dust-free minimum examples hain, poori list nahi. Exam trap: Rule 210 kis par zyada sakht hai? "Especially valuable and/or combustible articles" par — dono category high-risk hain.

Rule 211 — Lists and Accounts. Yaad rakho: Actual balance = Book balance, kisi bhi waqt check ho sake. Rule 211 do sub-rules aur ek Note mein hai. (i) general requirement — item-wise lists/accounts; (ii) chaar alag-alag registers; Note — forms mein aur detail jodi ja sakti hai. Clause (i): Do duties: item-wise lists + accounts rakhna, aur accurate returns banana. Asal test ye hai: kisi bhi waqt asal balance (physical) aur book balance (register) ki tulna ho sake. Clause (ii): Chaar category ke liye alag-alag accounts — ek hi register sab kuch nahi. Note: Departments in forms mein aur columns jod sakte hain (jaise warranty expiry, AMC details, location code). Par jo GFR likhta hai, wahan se hatna nahi — minimum to hona hi chahiye — supplement karna hai, replace karna nahi. Exam trap: Kaunsa form kis asset ke liye? GFR-22 Register of Fixed Assets, GFR-23 Stock Register of consumables, GFR-18 Accession Register (library books), GFR-24 Register of assets of historical/artistic value.

Rule 212 — Hiring out of Fixed Assets. Yaad rakho: Record + Regular recovery + Historical cost = Rule 212. Rule 212 bhi ek single paragraph hai — teen requirements: record, regular recovery, historical cost basis. Rule 212: Jab koi fixed asset (jaise departmental genset, machinery, vehicle, tentage) kisi local body, contractor ya kisi aur ko kiraye par diya jaaye, to teen cheezein: (1) asset ka proper record — kaunse asset, kisko, kab se kab tak; (2) hire aur dusre charges regularly recover karne honge — charges wahi jo competent authority ke prescribed rules ke under hain; (3) charges ki ganana historical cost par hogi — matlab asset jis price par kharida gaya tha (uski original cost), aaj ke market rate ya replacement cost par nahi. Note: Rule 212 khud koi rate prescribe nahi karta — rates "rules prescribed by the competent authority" se aate hain. Rule sirf basis (historical cost) fix karta hai. Exam trap: Hire charges kis par based honge? Historical cost par — market rate, replacement cost ya insurance value par nahi.

Rule 213 — Physical verification of Fixed Assets and Consumables. Yaad rakho: Ek saal, Dono category, Custodian saamne, Certificate, Discrepancy → R.33–38. Rule 213 teen sub-rules ka hai: 213(1) fixed assets, 213(2) consumables, 213(3) verification ka procedure (teen clauses). Isi rule se verification ki poori kahani chalti hai. Rule 213(1): Teen baatein: (a) fixed assets ka inventory ordinarily site par rahega — matlab jahan asset hai wahin record bhi, alag jagah file mein nahi; (b) verification kam se kam saal mein ek baar; (c) verification ka nateeja corresponding register mein darj ho. Rule 213(2): Consumables ka bhi wahi frequency — saal mein kam se kam ek baar — lekin nateeja stock register mein darj hoga, aur wahan se aage competent authority action legi. Note: Rule 213(3)(iii) Chapter 7 ko Chapter 2 ke "Defalcation and losses" (Rules 33–38) se jodta hai — shortage ka matlab automatic penalty nahi, balki reporting chain shuru hona hai. Exam trap: Fixed assets aur consumables — dono ki verification frequency? Dono "at least once in a year" (213(1) aur 213(2)).

Rule 214 — Buffer Stock. Yaad rakho: Buffer = authority tay kare, 1 saal se upar = generally surplus. Rule 214 ek chhota rule hai par iska Note poore chapter ka sabse cited line hai — "ek saal se zyada stock mein pada material generally surplus". Rule 214: Optimum buffer stock competent authority tay karega — ye koi fixed number nahi jo GFR mein likha ho. Tay karte waqt teen factors dekhne honge: requirement ki frequency, quantity, aur supply ka pattern (lead time, reliability). Matlab buffer stock ek analysis ka nateeja hai, guess nahi. Note: Ye note do kaam karta hai. Pehla: reasoning — inventory carrying cost aisa kharch hai jo material ki value nahi badhata, isliye bina wajah stock rakhna financial propriety ke khilaf hai. Exam trap: Buffer stock ka optimum level kaun tay karta hai? Competent authority — frequency, quantity aur supply pattern ke base par. GFR koi fixed figure nahi deta.

Rule 215 — Physical verification of Library books. Yaad rakho: 20,000 = har saal, 50,000 = 3 saal, usse upar = sample, 5 per 1,000. Rule 215 library books ke liye Rule 213 ka special exception hai — yahan do clauses hain: (i) verification ka scale-based schedule, (ii) reasonable loss ka norm. Clause (i): Teen slabs: ≤ 20,000 volumes → har saal complete verification; 20,000 se zyada aur 50,000 tak → kam se kam 3 saal mein ek baar complete verification; 50,000 se zyada → sample verification, jinke beech ka interval 3 saal se zyada na ho. Clause (ii): Pehla hissa ek concession hai: ek saal mein jitni books issue/consult hui unmein har 1,000 par 5 volumes ki loss reasonable maani ja sakti hai — par sirf tab jab woh dishonesty ya negligence ki wajah se na ho. Note: Rule 215 Rule 213 ke "at least once in a year" se exception hai — library books par scale-based schedule lagta hai, annual nahi (siwaye ≤20,000 volumes wale library ke). Exam trap: 30,000 volumes wale library mein verification? Complete verification kam se kam 3 saal mein ek baar.

Rule 216 — Transfer of charge of goods, materials etc.. Yaad rakho: Statement, Dono sign with date, Dono ke paas copy. Rule 216 ek paragraph ka rule hai — lekin yahi tay karta hai ki charge badalne ke baad kisi bhi kami ki zimmedari kiski hogi. Rule 216: Teen requirements: (1) jaane wala (transferred) officer ensure karega ki goods/materials sahi tareeke se successor ko hand over ho jayen — sirf chabi dena kaafi nahi; (2) ek statement banega jismein goods/materials ki saari relevant details hon, aur use relieving (charge lene wale) aur relieved (charge chhodne wale) dono officers date ke saath sign karenge; (3) dono ek-ek copy rakhenge. Note: Rule 216 mein koi proviso ya exception nahi — ye har transfer par lagta hai, chahe charge kitne din ka ho. Exam trap: Statement kaun sign karega? Relieving aur relieved — dono, date ke saath. Sirf ek ka sign kaafi nahi.

Rule 217 — Disposal of Goods. Yaad rakho: Declare → Record reasons → Value → GFR-10 → Responsibility → E-waste rules. Rule 217 paanch clauses ka hai aur poore disposal process ka pehla darwaza hai. Iske bina Rule 218 ka koi mode choose nahi kiya ja sakta. Clause (i): Declaration tab ho sakti hai jab item Ministry/Department ke kaam ka na rahe. Par declaration kaun karega — woh authority jo item kharidne ke liye competent hai (authority competent to purchase). Aur us authority ko reasons record karne hi honge. Clause (ii): Committee banana vivek-adhikar hai — "may, at his discretion". Matlab committee zaroori nahi, par bade ya sensitive lots ke liye banana behtar practice (aur aksar departmental instructions mein likha hota hai). Exam mein ye MAY vs SHALL ka favourite sawal hai. Clause (iii): Teen prices nikalne honge: book value, guiding price, reserved price. Agar book value nikalna sambhav na ho, to original purchase price use kiya ja sakta hai (yahan "may be utilised" ek permitted fallback hai). Note: Rule 217(v) GFR ko E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 aur MoEF&CC guidelines se jodta hai — isliye Special Campaign mein e-waste disposal ka alag se target hota hai. Exam trap: Item ko surplus/obsolete/unserviceable kaun declare karta hai? Woh authority jo item kharidne ke liye competent hai (authority competent to purchase), reasons record karke.

Rule 218 — Modes of Disposal. Yaad rakho: ₹4 lakh = Tender ya Auction, ₹2 lakh = 10.07.2024 se pehle. Rule 218 chaar clauses ka hai aur amended hai: clause (i) ki threshold DoE OM F.1/3/2024-PPD (10.07.2024) se ₹2 lakh se badhkar ₹4 lakh ho gayi. Clause (i): Assessed residual value (na ki original purchase value) ₹4,00,000 se upar ho to disposal sirf do tareeqon se: (a) advertised tender se bids, ya (b) public auction. DONO mein se koi ek chunna hai — teesra raasta (direct sale, quotation, committee decision) allowed nahi. Amendment: 10.07. Clause (ii): ₹4 lakh se kam residual value par mode competent authority tay karegi, lekin bina reason ke nahi — teen objectives dhyan mein rakhne honge: (1) samaan ka jama hona rokna, (2) jagah block na hona, (3) disposal hone wale samaan ki value kharab na hona. Clause (iii): Kuch cheezein bechi nahi ja sakti — expired medicines, food grain, ammunition jaise hazardous ya human consumption ke layak na hone wale items ko तुरंत dispose ya destroy karna hai, suitable mode se. Teen wajah: health hazard, environmental pollution, aur misuse ki sambhavna. Note: Clause (i) aur (ii) dono mein threshold ek hi hai aur dono amendment ke saath badalte hain — 10.07.2024 se pehle dono jagah ₹2 lakh tha. Amendment: [object Object] Exam trap: Current threshold kya hai? ₹4,00,000 assessed residual value (10.07.2024 se). Purani kitabon mein ₹2 lakh milega — wo outdated hai.

Rule 219 — Disposal through Advertised Tender. Yaad rakho: 9 steps (a)–(i), 7 aspects (a)–(g), 10% bid security, late bid = no. Rule 219 teen hisson mein hai: (i) nau broad steps (a) se (i), (ii) saat important aspects (a) se (g), aur (iii) late bids ka rule. Clause (i): Nau kadam: bidding document banana → tender invite karna → bids kholna → analysis/evaluation → highest responsive bidder chunna → sale value collect karna → sale release order dena → goods release karna → unsuccessful bidders ki bid security wapas karna. Clause (ii)(a): Chaar value: transparency, competition, fairness, discretion ka khatma. Sale plan aur goods ka wide publicity zaroori. Saari terms bidding document mein comprehensive, plain and simple language mein honi chahiye — chhupe hue conditions nahi. Aur taxes ka applicability document mein saaf likha ho. Clause (ii)(b): Bidding document mein goods ka location aur present condition dono likhne honge, taaki bidder bidding se pehle inspect kar sake. Isse "jo dekha wo mila" wala dispute nahi hota — isliye condition chhupana rule ke khilaf hai. Note: (i) mein nau steps hain (a)–(i), jabki (ii) mein saat aspects (a)–(g) — dono ki numbering alag hai, confuse na karein. Exam trap: Bid security kitni? Ordinarily assessed ya reserved price ka 10% — exact amount bidding document mein.

Rule 220 — Disposal through Auction. Yaad rakho: 25% spot earnest money, Cash ya DACR, IFW officer zaroori. Rule 220 paanch clauses ka hai: (i) kaun karayega, (ii) principles + publicity, (iii) auction shuru mein dobara ghoshna, (iv) hammer stroke + earnest money, (v) team mein IFW officer. Clause (i): Auction do tareeqe se ho sakti hai: khud (directly) ya approved auctioneers ke through. Dono valid hain — "approved auctioneers" ka matlab hai ki kisi bhi private auctioneer ko nahi, approved ko hi lena hai. Clause (ii): Principles wahi — transparency, competition, fairness, discretion ka khatma. Auction plan mein goods ki details, unka location aur sale ki terms hon, aur use utni hi wide publicity mile jitni advertised tender ko milti hai. Matlab chupke se auction karwana allowed nahi. Clause (iii): Auction shuru karte waqt ek baar phir ghoshit karein: goods ki condition, location, aur terms & conditions — ikathhe hue bidders ke faayde ke liye. Publicity mein likha hua phir se bolna zaroori hai, taaki koi bole "mujhe pata nahi tha". Note: 25% earnest money aur 10% bid security (Rule 219) mein farq yaad rakhiye — auction mein 25%, tender mein 10%. Exam trap: Auction mein earnest money kitni? Bid value ka kam se kam 25% — तुरंत, mauke par, cash ya DACR mein.

Rule 221 — Disposal at scrap value or by other modes. Yaad rakho: Tender fail → Auction fail → Scrap (CA + Finance) → Eco-friendly destruction. Rule 221 ek paragraph ka hai, par iski pre-condition sabse important hai — ye tabhi lagta hai jab advertised tender aur auction dono try karke dekh liye hon. Rule 221: Do stages. Stage 1: agar advertised tender ya auction ke bawajood item nahi bikta, to scrap value par becha ja sakta hai — par competent authority ki approval ke saath Finance division se consultation karke. Yani do alag cheezein: approval (competent authority) + consultation (Finance division). Note: Rule 221 "MAY" hai — lekin condition ke saath: pehle dono sale modes try karne honge. Exam trap: Kya bina tender/auction try kiye seedha scrap value par bech sakte hain? Nahi. "In spite of its attempts through advertised tender or auction" — pehle dono try zaroori.

Rule 222 — Sale Account. Yaad rakho: Form GFR-11, Sale supervise karne wale officer ke sign. Rule 222 ek line ka rule hai — disposal ke baad ka antim record. Chhota par audit mein sabse pehle yahi maanga jaata hai. Rule 222: Dispose kiye gaye goods ka sale account Form GFR-11 mein banega, aur us par us officer ke sign honge jisne sale ya auction ki supervision ki. Dhyan dein: sign karne wala wohi officer hai jisne supervise kiya — koi aur officer "on behalf" sign nahi kar sakta is rule ke under. Note: Rule 222 kisi bhi mode ke baad lagta hai — tender ho, auction ho ya scrap sale. Exam trap: Sale account kaun sign karta hai? Woh officer jisne sale/auction supervise kiya.

Rule 223 — Write-off of losses. Yaad rakho: Sanction har haal mein, 4 depreciation heads, 5 non-depreciation heads. Rule 223 teen sub-rules mein hai: (1) powers to write off, (2) depreciation wale losses ke 4 heads, (3) depreciation ke alawa wale losses ke 5 heads. Rule 223(1): Teen baatein: (1) revaluation, stock-taking ya kisi aur wajah se hone wale profit aur loss dono record kiye jayenge aur zaroorat padne par adjust kiye jayenge; (2) formal sanction competent authority ki leni hogi — chahe government accounts mein koi correction/adjustment ho ya na ho. Rule 223(2): Depreciation se hone wale loss ko chaar heads mein baant kar record karna hai: (i) market price ka normal utaar-chadhav; (ii) normal ghisavat (wear & tear); (iii) kharid regulate karne mein foresight ki kami; (iv) kharid ke baad negligence. Rule 223(3): Depreciation ke alawa wale losses ke paanch heads: (i) chori ya fraud; (ii) upeksha (neglect); (iii) obsolescence ya zarurat se zyada kharid ki anticipated losses; (iv) damage (nuksan); (v) Force Majeure — aag, baadh, dushman ki action jaise extraordinary situations. Note: Rule 223(1) ka "even though no formal correction or adjustment in government accounts is involved" — sabse zyada poocha jaane wala line. Exam trap: Accounts mein koi adjustment nahi hoga to bhi sanction chahiye? Haan — Rule 223(1) clear roop se kehta hai "even though no formal correction or adjustment in government accounts is involved".
